public_rationale: OpenAI's launch evaluations show hallucinations and incorrect answers even when the necessary information is supplied. That supports the narrow claim that these failures persisted. The same results show improvement, so this finding does not establish that GPT-4.5 was useless or that scaling had stopped working.
limitations: The benchmarks establish persistence, not the frequency of failures in ordinary use.
Stupid errors has no formal definition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4.5 did not eliminate hallucinations or stupid errors.

statement.excerpt: So now GPT 4.5 has dropped, and — breaking news — I was right. Hallucinations didn’t disappear today, and nor did stupid errors.
statement.document_title: Hot take: GPT 4.5 is a nothing burger

our_interpretation: Assess the model released on February 27, 2025.
The ordinary reading is that fabricated factual answers and obvious mistakes persisted. It does not imply that their frequency failed to improve.
Treat incorrect answers to questions whose answers are explicitly supplied as an ordinary example of an obvious mistake.
criteria.support_condition: Launch-model evaluations establish both nonzero hallucinations and errors on straightforward tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that the released model eliminated either claimed class of failure. Improved scores alone do not contradict persistence.

evidence.excerpt: We tested OpenAI GPT-4.5 against PersonQA, an evaluation that aims to elicit hallucinations.
evidence.explanation: The launch card reports a 0.19 PersonQA hallucination rate and 0.74 accuracy on unambiguous BBQ questions, where the answer is supplied in the prompt. These establish persistent hallucinations and straightforward answer-selection mistakes, although PersonQA improved over GPT-4o.
